title: Ausencia de rasgo oficial: 'carecer de + sustantivo' y 'interpretarse sin'

sections.content: One of the most famous facts about Spain's National Anthem ('el Himno Nacional de España') is expressed with 'carecer de + sustantivo' (to lack / have no) or 'no tener letra oficial': the Spanish anthem has NO official lyrics ('carece de letra oficial'). Known historically as the **Marcha Real** or **Marcha Granadera**, it is one of the oldest national anthems in Europe (documented in 1761 and declared Royal March of Honor by King Charles III in 1770) and is regulated today by Royal Decree 1560/1997.

items.spanish: El Himno Nacional de España es conocido tradicionalmente como la «Marcha Real» o «Marcha Granadera».
items.english: The National Anthem of Spain is traditionally known as the 'Marcha Real' or 'Marcha Granadera'.

items.spanish: A diferencia de la mayoría de los himnos nacionales, la Marcha Real carece de letra oficial.
items.english: Unlike most national anthems, the Marcha Real has no official lyrics.

items.spanish: Fue declarada Marcha de Honor por el rey Carlos III en el año 1770.
items.english: It was declared March of Honor by King Charles III in the year 1770.

sections.content: High-yield CCSE facts: 1) What is the name of Spain's national anthem? **La Marcha Real** (or **Marcha Granadera**). 2) Does it have official lyrics? **No, no tiene letra oficial**.
